meta.title: Unterm — a terminal AI agents can control
meta.desc: A cross-platform terminal built for agent control: drive panes, cwd, screenshots, and sessions through MCP, HTTP, and CLI.
cap.title: The complete control surface
cap.subtitle: Not a screenshot tour — the real surface every agent and script can call. 65 MCP methods across 11 namespaces, plus 22 CLI commands, all returning the same JSON.
cap.surfaces.note: Every method is reachable from MCP (JSON-RPC over TCP), the unterm-cli binary, the Web Settings HTTP API, and the GUI — one round-trip to meta.surface (or unterm-cli reference) returns this entire list live.
cap.session.title: Sessions & panes
cap.session.body: Spawn, split, focus, resize, and destroy panes from outside the terminal. Type into any pane character-by-character, read its cwd, poll until idle — no keystroke simulation.
cap.screen.title: Screen reading
cap.screen.body: Pull live viewport text, the full scrollback as one string, cursor position, or a regex search. detect_errors flags failed commands for an agent to react to.
cap.exec.title: Command execution
cap.exec.body: Run a command and stream output, run-and-wait for an exit code, send raw bytes, query status, cancel, or deliver a POSIX signal — structured results, not screen-scraping.
cap.agents.title: AI agent launcher
cap.agents.body: Install, authenticate, configure, and launch Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode / Aider. The mcp-stdio bridge auto-wires each one back to this terminal's MCP server.
cap.identity.title: Identity profiles
cap.identity.body: Bind a window to a developer identity — GitHub PAT, AWS keys, npm token, SSH key, git author. Credentials live in the OS vault; 7 sniffers discover existing ones read-only.
cap.instance.title: Multi-instance
cap.instance.body: Each window is a NATO-named instance (alpha, bravo, charlie…). Enumerate every live Unterm on the machine, focus one, or retitle it — an agent routes work across windows by cwd or title.
cap.rec.title: Recording & replay
cap.rec.body: Record any session as an asciicast, replay it, or export to OSC-133 block-segmented markdown with token redaction — each block carries its command, output, exit code, and duration.
cap.capture.title: Capture & upload
cap.capture.body: Screenshot the screen, a window, or a drag-selected region; read the clipboard; or push a file to your own Aliyun OSS / Tencent COS / Qiniu bucket and get back a public URL — all over MCP.
cap.proxy.title: Proxy management
cap.proxy.body: Read the OS proxy state, switch between configured nodes, latency-test endpoints, or apply / clear system proxy overrides (macOS scutil · Windows registry · Linux env) — zero URL pasting.
cap.gov.title: Governance & audit
cap.gov.body: Every agent write is logged with its identity; a write-confirmation policy gates first contact. Test policy decisions, run the built-in self-test suite, and read liveness/readiness flags.
cap.workspace.title: Workspaces
cap.workspace.body: Save the current window's full pane / tab layout, list saved layouts, and restore one — an agent can snapshot a working set and bring it back later.
cap.meta.title: Self-describing surface
cap.meta.body: meta.surface returns every MCP method (with param schemas), every CLI subcommand, and every live keybinding in one call — so an agent that just connected learns the whole API without docs.

stand.title: Where Unterm stands out
stand.subtitle: Three claims you can grep, build, or run yourself. No marketing fog.
stand.agents.title: The terminal you boot every AI coding CLI from
stand.agents.body: v0.18 makes Unterm a one-click launcher for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Aider. Each agent's install command, OAuth flow, API key, and native config file are described by a signed manifest fetched from unterm.app; the runtime drops the key into your OS keychain, writes the agent's own JSON/TOML/YAML config (preserving unknown fields), exposes Unterm itself to the agent as an MCP server, and records the session into audit — all reachable from the CLI and the new AI Agents Web Settings tab.
stand.split.title: AI splits panes from outside the terminal
stand.split.body: session.split + session.focus over MCP let an external agent (Claude Code, Cursor, your script) carve the active window left / right / up / down and hand focus to the new pane — without simulating any keystroke. Built into the Python snippet on the hero. No other terminal exposes pane geometry to outside processes this way.
stand.audit.title: Every agent write is auditable, revocable, reviewable
stand.audit.body: Each session.input / exec.send is logged with the calling agent's identity. First write from a new agent triggers an Allow / Block / Always-allow banner. Trust persists to ~/.unterm/trusted_agents.json and is one click revocable from the Web Settings MCP tab. The status bar shows live MCP write count.
stand.identity.title: One window per developer identity
stand.identity.body: Bind a window to a coherent identity in one shot: GitHub PAT, AWS keys, npm token, OpenAI key, SSH key, git author. Credentials live in the OS-native vault (Keychain / Credential Manager / libsecret) — never on disk. Seven sniffers read existing credentials so first-time setup is empty.
qol.title: Small touches that add up
qol.subtitle: Daily-driver polish — none are headline features, but together they remove friction.
qol.ghost.title: Cross-pane ghost text
qol.ghost.body: Fish-style grey prediction continues your input from any pane's shell history; <kbd class="text-[10px] font-mono px-1 rounded bg-zinc-800">→</kbd> or <kbd class="text-[10px] font-mono px-1 rounded bg-zinc-800">End</kbd> accepts.
qol.suggest.title: session.suggest bar
qol.suggest.body: Agents propose commands without touching the PTY — sit above the status bar; <kbd class="text-[10px] font-mono px-1 rounded bg-zinc-800">Tab</kbd> accepts, <kbd class="text-[10px] font-mono px-1 rounded bg-zinc-800">Alt+Enter</kbd> accept-and-run.
qol.copy.title: Region screenshot → clipboard
qol.copy.body: Drag-select any rectangle from the status bar; PNG to disk, image to clipboard, file path as text — all at once.
qol.themes.title: Theme + per-tab CWD
qol.themes.body: 9 bundled themes; unterm-cli theme set midnight changes them all live. Status bar shows active pane's $HOME-relative cwd.
qol.finder.title: Native right-click on macOS
qol.finder.body: Finder right-click → Open in Unterm. Uses the AppleScript Services extension — no in-app context menu chrome.
qol.profiles.title: Identity chip in status bar
qol.profiles.body: Active identity profile (GitHub PAT / AWS keys / npm token bound to this window) shows in the status bar; click to spawn the next profile.
qol.proxy.title: Zero-config proxy
qol.proxy.body: Reads macOS scutil / Windows registry / GNOME gsettings / env. One toggle on/off. No URL pasting.
qol.headers.title: OSC 133 block segmentation
qol.headers.body: Recordings split on shell prompt boundaries automatically. Each block has its command, output, exit code, duration — searchable.
sponsor.title: Support Unterm
sponsor.subtitle: One developer builds and maintains Unterm in their spare time. If it speeds up your daily work, a small sponsorship keeps the project alive.
sponsor.note: Sponsors get listed in the README and the in-app About dialog (with permission). No paywall, no premium tier — everything ships in the same MIT-licensed binary.
sponsor.gh.title: GitHub Sponsors
sponsor.gh.body: International monthly or one-time tier. Processed by Stripe via GitHub. Cancelable any time.
sponsor.paypal.title: PayPal one-tap
sponsor.paypal.body: Worldwide one-time tip. Choose any amount in your local currency.
hero.subtitle: Install, sign in, configure, and launch Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Aider — one click each. Pick your vendor subscription or bring your own API key, per agent, per identity. And because Unterm exposes itself via MCP, the agent you just launched can drive Unterm back.
hero.meta: Unified AI agent launcher · Local-first · No cloud · No login
tagline.title: AI controls the terminal. MCP makes it real.
tagline.body: Most terminals embed AI inside the binary. Unterm does the opposite: keep AI outside, expose the terminal as a surface that any external agent can grip via MCP. The terminal is the thing being controlled; the agent is the thing doing the work.
agents.title: Install every coding agent. One click each. No setup tax.
agents.subtitle: If you've ever tried to run more than one AI coding CLI side-by-side, you know the tax: npm install, OAuth flow, API key, ~/.config/<vendor>/<different format each>, env vars, profile separation. Unterm v0.18 collapses that into one settings tab + a CLI. No other terminal does this.
agents.card.install.title: Install in the GUI or via CLI
agents.card.install.body: Click Install on any agent card, or run unterm-cli agent install <id>. Unterm runs the right command for your platform (npm / pipx / etc.), verifies the binary lands on PATH, and re-detects automatically.
agents.card.auth.title: Subscription by default. BYO key opt-in.
agents.card.auth.body: Most agents ship with OAuth tied to a paid subscription (Claude Pro, ChatGPT Plus, Google AI Pro). Unterm defaults to that mode — no API key is ever silently injected. Switch to bring your own key or custom endpoint explicitly in the Configure form when you actually want per-token billing or a corporate gateway.
agents.card.signed.title: Ed25519-signed manifest catalog
agents.card.signed.body: The list of agents + their install commands isn't hard-coded into Unterm — it's a signed envelope served from unterm.app/api/agents/manifests. A compromise of the CDN can't push curl | sh to your machine; the public key is baked into every Unterm binary.
demo.title: One AI controls another AI through the terminal.
demo.subtitle: The outer agent owns the terminal session. It switches cwd, launches an inner coding agent in a pane, reads the logs, and keeps iterating until the repository is green.
demo.flow.1.title: Open the repo
demo.flow.1.body: The outer agent points the active pane at the project root so every command, log, and screenshot stays anchored to the same working directory.
demo.flow.2.title: Start the inner agent
demo.flow.2.body: It spawns a coding agent in a split pane, gives it the task, and lets that agent do the edit loop inside the terminal.
demo.flow.3.title: Read, retry, release
demo.flow.3.body: The outer agent reads test output and pane state, retries when needed, and only moves to commit or release when the terminal says the work is done.
reflexive.badge: Live snippet · same socket, both directions
reflexive.title: The terminal AI agents drive — including their own.
reflexive.subtitle: Below is a real session from this Unterm window. Claude Code, running in pane #0, called session.split over MCP to put pane #5 on the right half, session.focus to make it active, then typed commands into it character-by-character with session.input. Same TCP socket reads what the shell echoed back via screen.text. No special agent integration — vanilla JSON-RPC, ~30 lines of Python.
reflexive.caption: The agent that wrote this section ran exactly that snippet, then used screen.text to copy the right-hand output back into this HTML. The v0.18 tag visible above? Same agent pushed it 30 minutes ago. Read AND write on the same socket — that's the whole story.
persona.title: Three ways to use Unterm
persona.subtitle: We didn't build for one workflow. The MCP surface means each persona gets the same control plane through different entry points.
persona.ai.title: AI engineers
persona.ai.body: Drive multiple terminal panes from Claude Code, Cursor, or your own agent. Each pane is one task; your agent picks where to type. Multi-instance NATO names (alpha, bravo, charlie…) make routing across windows trivial.
persona.ai.bullets.1: Director / worker pattern: outer agent supervises inner agent in a pane
persona.ai.bullets.2: Long-running watcher: kick off a build, poll until idle, decide next step
persona.ai.bullets.3: Multi-pane orchestration: fan work across projects, aggregate results
persona.ai.bullets.4: Recording with token redaction for review and fine-tune
persona.ops.title: DevOps & SREs
persona.ops.body: Cron-friendly CLI for everything you can do in the GUI. unterm-cli ships in every release; pipe --json through anywhere downstream that wants raw JSON-RPC. Same surface for ops scripts, dashboards, runbooks.
persona.ops.bullets.1: Auto proxy detection: macOS scutil / Windows registry / GNOME gsettings
persona.ops.bullets.2: Headless screenshots and pane reads for incident docs
persona.ops.bullets.3: Recording → markdown for runbook generation, PII-redacted by default
persona.ops.bullets.4: No telemetry, no login, every server bound to 127.0.0.1
persona.power.title: Power users & OSS hackers
persona.power.body: MIT-licensed WezTerm fork with first-class agent integration. Patches accepted on GitHub. Build it yourself; the binary CLI ships in every release. Web Settings UI is a Tailwind + Alpine SPA — fork the page, change the colors.
persona.power.bullets.1: Universal arm64 + x86_64 macOS binary, signed with Developer ID
persona.power.bullets.4: 9 locales out of the box, system locale auto-detect

features.title: Four control surfaces, one engine
features.subtitle: Every Unterm window starts a local MCP server and an HTTP settings server. Read and write the same JSON state from any of them.
features.mcp.title: MCP server
features.mcp.body: Line-delimited JSON-RPC on 127.0.0.1:19876, auth-token gated. Spawn shells, read pane state, capture screenshots, control sessions.
features.cli.title: unterm-cli
features.cli.body: Same surface from any shell, cron job, or script. Thin JSON-RPC client over the local MCP — no duplicated business logic.
features.web.title: Web Settings
features.web.body: Modern config UI in the browser, not the cell grid. Tailwind + Alpine SPA at 127.0.0.1:19877. Themes, proxy, recordings, language.
features.i18n.title: 9 languages
features.i18n.body: en / 简体 / 繁體 / 日本語 / 한국어 / Deutsch / Français / Italiano / हिन्दी out of the box. System locale auto-detect.
features.rec.title: Session recording
features.rec.body: OSC 133 block-segmented markdown with built-in redaction. Recordings live in <cwd>/.unterm/sessions/.
features.shot.title: Region screenshots
features.shot.body: One-click region capture from the status bar. PNG to disk, image to clipboard, path to text clipboard.
features.proxy.title: Auto proxy detect
features.proxy.body: Reads macOS scutil / Windows registry / GNOME gsettings / env. One-toggle on/off. No URL config.
features.engine.title: GPU rendering
features.engine.body: Built on a customized WezTerm engine — Metal on macOS, OpenGL on Linux, DirectX via ANGLE on Windows.
whatsnew.title: What's new in v0.38
whatsnew.uipolish.title: A more polished look out of the box + a new logo
whatsnew.uipolish.body: v0.38 is a visual pass on the defaults. Content gets room to breathe (window padding 4px → 16/16/10/8), the bundled JetBrains Mono with ligatures is now the default font (no more falling back to whatever monospace the system happens to have), line-height opens up to 1.15, and the warm Notion Dark scheme is the default on fresh installs — window chrome and the tab bar are warmed to the same palette so nothing clashes. The app icon is redesigned too: a warm-black monogram where a teal U cradles an amber T over a terminal block cursor. Deeper polish — active-pane treatment, status-bar grouping, a tasteful default prompt — is queued for the next round.
whatsnew.rotationfix.title: Auto-rotation that never drops your network
whatsnew.rotationfix.body: Proxy auto-rotation used to fail over on a single slow health check — one jittery probe and your exit node got yanked out mid-connection, dropping logged-in sessions, long downloads, and SSH. v0.37 makes failover deliberate: the active node is retried within each check and must miss two consecutive checks before Unterm switches; the health-probe timeout widens to 5s and the minimum interval to 10s. A transient hiccup no longer rotates the whole system's proxy out from under your terminal — rotation fires only when a node is genuinely dead. It honors the rule that has governed proxy support from day one: the proxy must never break the terminal. Drive it from the Web Settings rotation pool or unterm-cli proxy rotation.
whatsnew.aicomplete.title: Type any AI CLI flag — Unterm finishes it inline
whatsnew.aicomplete.body: Building on the per-CLI flag catalog, v0.34 brings full flag and argument ghost-text completion for the AI coding CLIs. Start typing claude --, codex --, gemini --, opencode --, or aider -- in any pane and Unterm completes the flag name inline — and where the flag takes a known value (model names, approval modes, sandbox levels) it predicts the argument too — as grey ghost text. → / Tab accepts. The completions come from the same signed manifest catalog that drives the Launch-options checkboxes, so the inline predictor and the GUI never drift apart.
whatsnew.winclash.title: Zero-config Clash detection on Windows
whatsnew.winclash.body: Proxy rotation reads your Clash / mihomo nodes through the controller API — but Windows has no Unix socket, so v0.33 auto-discovers the TCP external-controller address + secret from the usual Clash Verge / mihomo config locations under %APPDATA% / %LOCALAPPDATA%. Rotation now works out of the box on Windows exactly as it does on macOS and Linux. Also in v0.33: turning rotation on now switches the proxy on if it was off (no more silently-armed-but-idle rotation), and AI-CLI command-name completion joins the flag/argument ghost text.
whatsnew.launchflags.title: Pick an AI CLI's flags — Unterm autocompletes them
whatsnew.launchflags.body: Each AI coding CLI has dozens of launch flags (model, sandbox, approval-mode, skip-trust, yolo, …) and remembering the names is friction. v0.23 ships a per-CLI flag catalog in the manifest — 22 flags across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Aider, each with an i18n label, a description, and a risk tag (safe / caution / danger). The catalog drives three surfaces from one source: Web Settings → AI Agents → Launch options renders the catalog as risk-colored checkboxes (⚠ on auto-approve flags; never pre-checked); the saved selection composes into the launch command for both the GUI and unterm-cli agent launch; and when you type gemini -- in any pane, Unterm's ghost-text predictor completes the flag name inline (→ / Tab accepts). The aggressive --yolo / --dangerously-skip-permissions family is exposed as opt-in only, so the audit design isn't undermined by a forced default. Also in v0.23: agent install now works from the Dock-launched Unterm on macOS (resolves npm/pipx via Homebrew, npm-global, nvm/fnm, …) and on Windows (npm.cmd shim invocation); the unterm-cli reference CLI registry is resynced to the real clap surface (theme switch, lang current, full profile / agent / proxy subcommands); selftest.run no longer false-fails on macOS/Linux; and the live unterm.app/api/agents/manifests envelope was republished so the v0.22 autowire fix (.mcp.json path, Gemini autowire) finally reaches online users.
whatsnew.clashrotate.title: Proxy rotation that reads your nodes — you just tick the boxes
whatsnew.clashrotate.body: v0.30 shipped endpoint-level rotation; v0.31 makes it actually useful. Unterm now talks to your proxy software's Clash / mihomo controller (over its Unix socket or TCP API — Clash, Clash Verge, ClashX, mihomo, sing-box), reads your real node groups and nodes with live latency + reachability, and lets you tick which ones to rotate among — no hand-typing endpoint URLs. When the active node stops responding, Unterm delay-tests the pool and switches the group to the fastest live pick, all through the controller API. Non-Clash setups fall back to manual endpoint nodes. Also in v0.31: the scrollbar now follows the active pane in a split — it sits on whichever pane has focus, instead of always pinning to the window edge.
whatsnew.rotation.title: Proxy auto-rotation — and a terminal that never silently loses the network
whatsnew.rotation.body: v0.30 adds endpoint-level proxy auto-rotation: pick a pool of nodes in the proxy panel and Unterm health-checks the active one, failing over to the fastest reachable node the moment it dies. It's software-agnostic — endpoint-level failover, so it works with any Clash / V2Ray / sing-box setup and survives you switching proxy apps. Just as important, proxy injection is now liveness-probed before it touches a shell: if the configured proxy port isn't accepting connections, Unterm injects nothing and the terminal stays on a direct connection instead of routing every command into a black hole — a dead proxy can no longer look like "my VPN broke". Drive it all from the Web Settings pool checkboxes or unterm-cli proxy rotation. Also in v0.30: a clean window-edge scrollbar (on by default, themed thumb), the warm Notion-Dark theme across the whole app and website, and a roomier settings menu.
whatsnew.autodiscovery.title: Every AI agent on your machine auto-discovers Unterm — now native on ARM too
whatsnew.autodiscovery.body: v0.22 wired up agents that Unterm launches. v0.24 closes the other half: on first launch (per version) Unterm registers its unterm MCP server into every AI coding agent installed on the machine — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode — by merging into each one's global config (never clobbering; an existing-but-unparseable config is refused, not overwritten) and dropping a short marker-delimited note into their CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / GEMINI.md. So even an agent you started in some other terminal knows Unterm is here and can drive it. The mcp-stdio bridge self-discovers the live instance, so a static registration keeps working across restarts and multi-window. Run unterm-cli setup-ai any time to re-sync, --remove to undo; connected agents also get a usage brief via the MCP initialize instructions field. Also in v0.24: native ARM64 builds. Unterm now ships five targets — macOS, Windows x64 + arm64, Linux x64 + arm64 — each built natively in CI on its own architecture, with arm64 ConPTY + ANGLE bundled for Windows-on-ARM.
whatsnew.autowire.title: Agents auto-wire to Unterm's MCP on launch
whatsnew.autowire.body: Launch Claude Code / Codex / Gemini / OpenCode from Unterm and they come pre-connected to this terminal's MCP server — no manual config. A new unterm-cli mcp-stdio bridge speaks the MCP stdio protocol and proxies every call to the running instance's control server, so the launcher can write each agent's native MCP config (.mcp.json for Claude Code, ~/.codex/config.toml for Codex, ~/.gemini/settings.json for Gemini, opencode.json for OpenCode — each in its own correct schema, merged not clobbered) pointing at the bridge. The agent can drive the terminal it lives in from its first prompt. Also in v0.22: split-focus is now shown by a thin accent bar on the active pane (no more harsh frame), the per-pane scrollbar no longer bleeds into the status bar, and the Notion Light / Notion Dark themes finally show + apply correctly from Web Settings.
whatsnew.reference.title: One MCP call now returns every method, every CLI, every shortcut
whatsnew.reference.body: A new meta.surface MCP method + unterm-cli reference + a Reference tab in Web Settings — same JSON behind all three. An agent that just connected gets the full surface (60+ MCP methods with param schemas, 22 CLI subcommands, every currently-bound keybinding read live from your unterm.lua) in one round trip; users can search it locally without leaving Settings. The MCP method list is now the source of truth for both server.capabilities and dispatch — adding a new method requires updating one registry, no more drift between dispatch and the published catalog. unterm-cli reference --section keys --filter copy for a quick local cheatsheet; --section mcp / cli for the others.
whatsnew.agentdump.title: Two more ways to hand a pane to an AI
whatsnew.agentdump.body: Two paired pieces that close the agent-handoff loop without dragging files around. (1) screen.scrollback_text MCP + unterm-cli scrollback dump the full pane history + viewport as a single string — strictly better than a rendered "long screenshot" for LLM hand-off: parses natively, no OCR, no font fidelity loss, optional ANSI escapes for color-aware analysis. (2) upload.file MCP + unterm-cli upload <file> push a local file to your own Aliyun OSS / Tencent COS / Qiniu Kodo bucket and return a public URL. Credentials live in ~/.unterm/upload.json and never leave the box — signing is hand-rolled HMAC-SHA1 so we don't drag in any vendor SDK. Together with capture.window, an agent can screenshot → upload → embed the URL in one round trip. Plus: new Notion Light / Notion Dark / Classic Dark color schemes with an active-pane outline that survives split focus, and a Windows fix that clears a stuck SPI_SETSCREENREADER flag so PSReadLine and bracketed paste keep working when another app forgets to reset it.
whatsnew.windowtitle.title: Window titles lead with project name
whatsnew.windowtitle.body: Open three Unterm windows for three projects and the Dock / Cmd-Tab / Mission Control window-list used to show Unterm — alpha — zsh for all of them — same prefix, indistinguishable. v0.19 flips to Apple's <Document> — <App> convention and leads with the project directory basename: unterm — Unterm (alpha), solomd — Unterm (bravo). The NATO instance id moves to a trailing parenthesis so screenshot-OCR agents still get the mapping back to ~/.unterm/instances/<id>.json. Explicit user overrides (set via unterm-cli instance set-title or MCP) still take priority.
whatsnew.subtitle: Proxy auto-rotation that survives flaky nodes, full ghost-text completion for every AI CLI's flags and arguments, and zero-config Clash detection on Windows — the most recent releases, in four cards.
whatsnew.agents.title: AI Agent integration: 5 first-party CLIs, one click each
whatsnew.agents.body: Install / authenticate / configure / launch any of Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, or Aider directly from Unterm's Web Settings or `unterm-cli agent ...`. Each agent is described by a signed manifest (Ed25519, served from unterm.app/api/agents/manifests, with a baked fallback so offline installs still work). Settings are schema-driven: edit them in a typed form and Unterm writes the agent's native config file with `preserve_unknown_keys` semantics; API keys land in the OS keychain via the existing identity profile. New Shell → AI Agents menu spawns each one in a fresh tab with the right env injected. Every launched session lands in the audit index tagged agent_id / manifest_version / profile.
whatsnew.reflexive.title: session.split + session.focus + an MCP trust panel
whatsnew.reflexive.body: Three pieces that close the loop on "AI drives the terminal — including its own." session.split lets an agent split a pane left/right/up/down without simulating a keystroke; session.focus makes the new pane active so the hand-off is visible to the user. Both are exercised in the live snippet above. Web Settings gains a new MCP tab: a runtime trust list (with per-agent write counts and one-click revoke) plus the last 80 audited write attempts in a sortable table. Trust persists to ~/.unterm/trusted_agents.json so Alt+A survives a restart. New /docs/agent-recipes page collects 9 copy-pastable Python snippets.
whatsnew.aiterminal.title: Agent-aware terminal — audit, suggest, ghost text
whatsnew.aiterminal.body: Three pieces fall into place to make Unterm a real AI-collaboration terminal. (1) Every session.input / exec.send is audited; the first time a new agent writes to a pane, a blocking banner asks the user — [Enter] allow, [Esc] block, [Alt+A] always-allow. The new mcp:N chip in the status bar tracks cumulative MCP PTY writes; click to copy the audit log. (2) session.suggest lets agents propose text without ever touching the PTY directly — a ✨ suggest bar sits above the status bar, [Tab] accepts, [Esc] dismisses, [Alt+Enter] accepts and runs. (3) Fish-style grey ghost text continues your input from cross-pane shell history; [→] / [End] accepts the prediction. All three keystrokes (Tab, Esc, Enter) pass through to the shell when no banner / suggestion / prediction is showing — vim, less, fzf all keep working unchanged.
whatsnew.configfix.title: Config resilience — unknown fields no longer crash
whatsnew.configfix.body: Setting an unrecognized key in your unterm.lua (e.g. a future or experimental option) used to abort the process on Windows release builds. The Lua FFI callback crossed a panic = abort boundary and triggered an unrecoverable crash with no diagnostic. v0.15 defaults config_builder() to non-strict mode: unknown fields produce a visible warning and the app continues to start normally.
whatsnew.profiles.title: Identity profiles — one window per identity
whatsnew.profiles.body: Bind a window to a coherent developer identity in one shot: GitHub PAT, AWS keys, npm token, OpenAI key, git author, SSH key routing. Tokens live in the OS-native vault (Keychain / Credential Manager / libsecret), never in ~/.unterm/. Seven sniffers (gh / aws / npm / ssh / docker / gcloud / netrc) discover existing credentials read-only. CLI + read-only MCP namespace expose the system to agents that need to know which identity is running. New chip in the status bar tells you at a glance — click to spawn a new window in the next profile.
whatsnew.flash.title: Sync pre-show paint kills the Windows white flash
whatsnew.flash.body: Three iterations to root-cause it: the DWM samples its redirection bitmap before WM_ERASEBKGND fires, so any fix routed through the message pump arrives too late. v0.12 renders one synchronous frame of real terminal content into the backbuffer in wezterm-gui before window.show(). Spawn-to-visible is ~880ms, no flash. Linux/macOS paths unchanged — the new path is cfg(windows) gated.
whatsnew.instances.title: Multi-instance NATO names
whatsnew.instances.body: Each Unterm process owns one instance with a NATO-phonetic name (alpha, bravo, charlie…). MCP instance.list enumerates all live instances; agents pick by cwd, title, or start order. Window title becomes Unterm — alpha — Project for visual mapping.
whatsnew.utf8.title: Auto UTF-8 on Windows
whatsnew.utf8.body: PowerShell and cmd.exe spawned by Unterm get UTF-8 output by default — no more mojibake on zh-CN, ja-JP, ko-KR Windows installs. Agents don't have to fix the user's $PROFILE; we wrap at spawn time with chcp 65001 + Console.OutputEncoding setup.
whatsnew.cwd.title: CWD in the status bar
whatsnew.cwd.body: Active pane's working directory shows up between the shell name and dimensions, with $HOME → ~ and middle truncation. Click to copy the full path. Works across local panes, mux clients, and SSH-forwarded sessions.
principles.title: Six principles, no exceptions
principles.local.title: Local-first, no cloud
principles.local.body: Every server, every API endpoint, every recording lives on 127.0.0.1. No login, no telemetry, no subscription. Your shell history is yours.
principles.outside.title: AI lives outside the terminal
principles.outside.body: No chat overlay, no ghost-text autocomplete, no inline AI panel. The terminal is the surface — Claude Code, Cursor, your scripts grip it through MCP.
principles.mcp.title: MCP is a first-class surface
principles.mcp.body: Every product feature ships with an MCP method and a CLI subcommand on day one. If it can't be driven from outside, it doesn't ship.
principles.parity.title: Cross-platform parity is correctness
principles.parity.body: A feature that works on Windows but bails on macOS or Linux is a bug, not a 'not yet supported.' Mac, Linux, Windows ship together.
principles.subtraction.title: Subtraction over decoration
principles.subtraction.body: When a feature belongs to the OS, use the OS. No in-terminal custom right-click chrome, no Cmd+Q confirmation, no manual proxy URL config — Finder integration now uses the native right-click extension and Services.
principles.subscription.title: Respect the subscription. Default OAuth.
principles.subscription.body: When you install an AI agent through Unterm, the default authentication mode is the vendor's official subscription (OAuth) — your Pro / Plus / Team plan. We never silently inject an API key into a session; per-token billing happens only if you explicitly switch the auth mode to 'bring your own API key' or 'custom endpoint' in the Configure form. This is an opt-in, not a footgun.
cmp.title: Unterm vs. a native terminal vs. a paid AI terminal
cmp.subtitle: The native terminal (Terminal.app) is the baseline you already have. Warp is the paid AI terminal. iTerm2 and Ghostty are the free power terminals. Unterm sits in its own lane: everything an external agent can grip from outside.
cmp.r.autowire: Agents auto-wire to the terminal's MCP
cmp.legend: ✓ yes · ✗ no · ~ partial · ×N count. The ✗ by design on "AI inside" is the whole thesis: Unterm keeps the AI outside and exposes the terminal as the surface it grips.
cmp.note: Reflects publicly documented features as of 2026-05. Warp is closed-source with a cloud-backed free tier + paid Team/Pro plans; iTerm2 ships a Python scripting API and an opt-in AI command plugin; Ghostty has no Windows build yet. Corrections welcome on GitHub.
dl.title: Get Unterm 0.23
dl.subtitle: macOS bundle is signed with a Developer ID and Apple-notarized. Linux .deb / AppImage and Windows .msi / .zip are also published.
faq.title: Frequently asked
faq.what.a: A cross-platform terminal emulator with built-in MCP, HTTP, and CLI control surfaces. The product thesis: terminal as MCP-controllable surface, so any external AI agent can drive it from outside instead of having an AI baked into the terminal itself.
faq.mcp.q: How does it work with Claude Code, Cursor, or other agents?
faq.mcp.a: Each Unterm window starts a local MCP server (TCP, JSON-RPC, auth-token gated). Point your MCP client at 127.0.0.1:<port> — the port + token are written to ~/.unterm/server.json on launch. The agent can spawn shells, run commands, read pane state, capture screenshots, toggle recording, and switch settings.
faq.multi.q: How do I drive multiple Unterm windows from one agent?
faq.multi.a: Each Unterm process is one instance with a NATO-phonetic name (alpha, bravo, …) recorded in ~/.unterm/instances/<name>.json. Call instance.list on any one of them to enumerate; pick by cwd / title / start order; connect to that instance's port with its auth token. ~/.unterm/active.json points at the most recent live instance for single-instance fallbacks.
faq.warp.q: How is this different from Warp?
faq.warp.a: Warp embeds AI inside a closed cloud orchestrator (Oz) — external tools like Claude Code can't drive Warp from outside. Unterm picks the third lane: keep AI out of the terminal, expose the terminal itself as an MCP-controllable surface, and let any agent grip it. No cloud, no login.
faq.privacy.a: Nowhere external. MCP and Web Settings servers bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Session recordings land under <project>/.unterm/sessions/ with built-in redaction for tokens. There is no telemetry, no analytics, no login, no cloud round-trip. Your shell history is yours.
faq.telemetry.q: Does Unterm phone home, even once?
faq.telemetry.a: No. Zero telemetry by default — not even an opt-in dialog. The only outbound HTTP requests Unterm makes are: (1) at user request, when you click a download link in Web Settings; (2) by your shell, like normal — anything your terminal would do, it still does. We don't ship analytics, error reporting, install pings, or update checks.
faq.cost.q: Is there a paid tier or premium feature?
faq.cost.a: No. Unterm is MIT-licensed; the same single binary ships every feature. No subscription, no Pro tier, no plugin marketplace, no "buy now to unlock split panes." If you'd like to support the project, the Sponsor section above is the only ask.
faq.size.q: How big is the install and runtime?
faq.size.a: macOS DMG ~117 MB · Linux .deb 35 MB · AppImage 46 MB · Windows MSI 44 MB. At idle with one window open, resident memory is ~110 MB; scales linearly per pane. Built on a customized WezTerm engine (GPU rendering: Metal / OpenGL / DirectX) — the binary is bigger than a barebones terminal but the runtime cost is dominated by your shell, not the renderer.
faq.locale.q: Does Unterm detect my system language?
faq.locale.a: Yes. On first launch, Unterm reads the OS locale (defaults on macOS, $LANG on Linux, registry on Windows) and picks the closest of 9 bundled UI languages. You can override per window in Web Settings → Language. Translations live in wezterm-gui/src/i18n/locales/*.json — patches welcome.
faq.agents_run.q: What stops a rogue agent from running rm -rf on my repo?
faq.agents_run.a: Three gates: (1) MCP server only listens on 127.0.0.1 — no network access. (2) Auth-token gated; the token is in ~/.unterm/instances/<name>.json, an agent without read access to that file can't even connect. (3) First write from a new agent triggers a blocking Allow / Block / Always-allow banner; the audit log records every write attempt with calling agent's identity. You can revoke trust at any time from the Web Settings MCP tab.
faq.script.a: Use unterm-cli: session list, proxy status, theme set midnight, session record start, screenshot. Pass --json to any subcommand for raw JSON-RPC output suitable for shell pipelines and cron jobs.
faq.platform.q: Which platforms ship signed and notarized?
faq.platform.a: macOS: universal arm64 + x86_64 DMG signed with a Developer ID and Apple-notarized + stapled (no Gatekeeper warnings). Linux: .deb for Debian/Ubuntu and AppImage for any distro. Windows: WiX-built MSI installer and portable .zip. All published to GitHub Releases on every minor tag.
faq.opensrc.a: Yes — MIT licensed. Built on top of the WezTerm engine for renderer / font / SSH / mux work, with a thin Unterm product layer (MCP, Web Settings, recording, i18n, signing pipeline) on top. Source at github.com/zhitongblog/unterm.
faq.contrib.a: Open an issue or PR on GitHub. The project tracks bugs, feature requests, and discussion in one queue. We bundle accumulated fixes into minor releases — patch-level versions don't trigger CI builds. Documentation lives in-repo at /docs.
